Based on my investigation, I have identified the root cause of the problem. The clickhouse-2 pod is stuck in ContainerCreating because the storage array has hit its maximum LUN mapping limit on that node. This is a storage infrastructure issue that requires administrative action outside of Kubernetes.

Let me update the ticket with the findings and recommended resolution:

input.note:
ROOT CAUSE: clickhouse-2 is stuck in ContainerCreating due to a storage array error. The pod's volume mount is failing with error "CVN-4127: host initiator iqn.1994-05.com.redhat:ip-10-0-93-12 rejected by array cv-array-02: host group hg-k8s-prod reached max LUN mappings (512); retry after mapping cleanup". This indicates the Corvane storage array (cv-array-02) has reached its maximum 512 LUN mapping limit for the host group hg-k8s-prod.

EVIDENCE: Pod status shows clickhouse-2 on node ip-10-0-93-12 with persistent volume claim data-clickhouse-2 (pvc-8d21f6c3-2a9e-4b07-9f4d-3e6a1c5b8d90) in Bound state, but the MountVolume operation is failing at the CSI driver level.

RESOLUTION: This requires storage infrastructure team intervention. The Corvane array administrator needs to clean up existing LUN mappings on the cv-array-02 array for host group hg-k8s-prod to free up space below the 512 mapping limit. Once mappings are cleaned up on the storage array side, the kubelet will retry the mount operation and the pod should transition to Running state. Contact your storage team to perform the cleanup on cv-array-02.
